name: Harbour link: a two-language service notice
project: A fictional small ferry operator posts a printed notice at both ends of a pedestrian crossing. This is an authored project fixture, not an actual service announcement.
audience: Residents, visiting passengers and older regular users who may be standing in a queue. English and French have equal information priority.
medium: A5 portrait notice, evaluated here as a 740 px print-preview. Pixel output is not evidence of actual print quality or viewing-distance performance.
tone: Calm, trustworthy, practical and welcoming. The interruption must be understood quickly without making the notice look like an emergency.
main_task: Recognize the temporary timetable, understand that the next boat uses the east landing, and distinguish outbound and return departure times.
language: Separate English and French blocks, with accents preserved. Do not shorten, translate or remove the supplied copy.
hierarchy: Service label, change headline, date range, bilingual explanation, departure rows, then assistance contact. Times should be easy to compare.
surroundings: Dark ink on warm white paper; one teal rule and pale grey timetable rows. No photography. Keep the supplied colors and overall block order.
existing_baseline: The exact current regular/bold family is supplied in context/baseline.json. It is coherent and already functional. Retaining that family, adjusting its sizes, or using one family throughout is a fully valid outcome.
design_freedom: Choose typography and, if necessary, revise the provided role sizes by at most 15% and line height from 1.2 to 1.6. Keep width 740, padding 42, text, colors and block order. Prefer no more than two families; justify any third.
acceptance: All supplied English/French copy and punctuation is covered and correctly shaped without fallback.
The exact final regular and emphasis styles are reproducible; synthetic bold/italic is disallowed.
No ink is clipped, no blocks overlap, and content fits within 1200 px height at width 740.
Outbound and return labels are distinguishable and the digits 1, 7 and 0 are visually checked in the actual timetable.
Record whether a replacement materially improved anything over the supplied baseline; novelty alone is insufficient.
